title: Unit-shift coherence of a roof-normalized natural RHom comparison
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $M\in\mathcal A$, $v=\operatorname{Hom}(M,-)$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathrm{Ab})$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and $S=M[0]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\psi_X^n:H^n(Rv(X))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(S,X[n])$ is any family satisfying the naturality equation and every-injective-resolution cocycle roof formula of [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof]. Let $F=\iota_{\mathrm{Ab}}\circ Rv$ send $X$ to the underlying derived abelian-group complex of $Rv(X)$, and let $\sigma_X:F(X[1])\to F(X)[1]$ be its canonical shift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Let $\chi_X^n$ be $H^n(\sigma_X)$ followed by the canonical homology shift comparison $H^n(F(X)[1])\simeq H^{n+1}(F(X))$. Let $\kappa_X:\iota(X[1])\to\iota(X)[1]$ be the inclusion shift comparison and $c_X^n:(X[1])[n]\to X[n+1]$ the inverse shift-addition comparison. Then for every $X$, integer $n$ and $b\in H^n(Rv(X[1]))$, $\psi_X^{n+1}(\chi_X^n(b))=c_X^n\circ\kappa_X[n]\circ\psi_{X[1]}^n(b)$. This concerns shifting one object and has no triangle or third morphism.

proof.text: Choose k with X cohomologically bounded below by k. Mathlib DerivedCategory.Plus.exists_injective_nonempty_iso gives an injective complex I and e:Q(I)≅X. Pull b back along e^{-1}[1]. On K=I[1], concrete cycles map onto cohomology: abCyclesIso.inv is an isomorphism, homologyπ is epi, homologyFunctorObjQIso.inv is an isomorphism, the derived unit is an isomorphism because every term of K is injective, and the quotient shift comparison eK is an isomorphism. Their composite g is epi and therefore surjective in AddCommGrpCat. Choose a cycle z mapping to the pulled-back class. Apply the single-cocycle shift equation and replace g(z) by that class.

Apply the assumed naturality at e in degree n+1 and at e[1] in degree n. Apply homology shiftMap to the naturality equation for the shift comparison of RV followed by inclusion; shiftMap_comp and shiftMap_comp' give the commuting cohomology square. The pulled-back class maps back to b because e is an isomorphism. Substitute the representative equation. Naturality of the inclusion shift comparison and the inverse shift-addition isomorphism identifies the two final postcompositions.
